title: Goal
description: What the user wants the software to do, expressed as an observable end state. Veridian never chooses the goal; it only validates against one.

statement.description: One sentence. Must describe an observable end state, not an activity.

context.description: Optional prose. Never load-bearing — if a criterion depends on it, the criterion is underspecified.

acceptance.description: Path to the acceptance contract, relative to the goal file.

environment.description: Path to the environment definition, relative to the goal file.

Limits.description: Safety boundaries (PLAN.md §52). Veridian executes potentially untrusted code, so every limit has a hard ceiling as well as a default.

networkAllowList.description: The origins `networkPolicy: allow-list` permits. A policy without its parameter is not a policy, so the list is a limit in its own right: without it, `allow-list` is indistinguishable from `deny`. Optional rather than required because `deny` and `allow` have no list to give, and requiring `[]` from them every time would be ceremony that teaches operators to paste an empty array without reading it.
